survival.title: Overall survival
survival.description: Radiomics-only Cox proportional-hazards model predicting time to death from any cause.
survival.targetDefinition: OS_STATUS / OS_MONTHS from the Duke demography sheet (1 = death, 0 = censored at last contact); missing status/time or non-positive follow-up excluded. Disease-specific, disease-free, and progression-free survival fields exist in the source workbook but are empty for every patient, so only overall survival is modeled.
survival.prevalenceNote: Death is uncommon in this cohort; the log-rank comparison and concordance interval both reflect that sparsity.

method.title: Cohort & label audit
method.detail: One row per patient; exact ID join; missing survival status, missing follow-up time, or non-positive follow-up excluded.

method.title: Radiomics-only matrix
method.detail: 2,064 tumor and peritumoral-vessel features; menopause and receptor fields explicitly removed.

method.title: Training-fold screen
method.detail: Univariate concordance-index ranking (k = 25, 50, 100), then |Spearman ρ| ≥ 0.90 redundancy pruning.

method.title: Sparse conventional model
method.detail: Z-score scaling and elastic-net (L1-weighted) Cox proportional-hazards regression; penalizer tuned in the inner loop.

method.title: Nested validation
method.detail: 5-fold × 3 repeated outer CV, 3-fold inner tuning, pooled out-of-fold risk scores, 1,000 bootstrap intervals.

method.title: Stability ranking
method.detail: Features ranked by outer-fold selection frequency, standardized coefficient magnitude, and univariate hazard ratio.

guardrails: Exploratory retrospective analysis—not a clinical decision tool.
No external cohort is supplied; internal cross-validation cannot establish transportability.
The strict response field is used as a pCR proxy and should be verified against the source data dictionary and pathology definition.
No repeat scans, segmentations, scanner/protocol metadata, or acquisition sites were available for ICC, perturbation testing, or ComBat harmonization.
Feature stability under segmentation variability and batch effects remains unknown.
Intervals summarize pooled out-of-fold predictions and do not fully capture uncertainty from all preprocessing choices.

Only 50 deaths were observed among 560 evaluable patients for the survival model; this event count limits the precision of the concordance interval more than the sample size alone suggests, and only overall survival could be modeled since disease-specific/disease-free/progression-free fields are empty in the source data.
